newsitem.title: UK: LCR rail hires director for 1998 flotation project.
newsitem.headline: LCR rail hires director for 1998 flotation project.

text.p: The LCR consortium operating Britain's Eurostar intercity passenger trains and planning to build a high speed rail link between London and the Channel Tunnel, said on Monday it had appointed a director to take charge of a project to prepare it for flotation.

London & Continental Railways (LCR), said in a statement it had hired Richard Aitken-Davies, who was recently responsible for coordinating the flotation of privatised railway infrastructure company Railtrack Plc.
LCR has currently scheduled its flotation for 1998.

It has not yet started work on the multi-billion stg construction work for the 67-mile (108 km) link but is seeking to build up its revenue base from its stake in the Eurostar network linking London, Paris and Brussels by express passenger trains through the tunnel.

LCR's main shareholders include U.S. civil engineer Bechtel, investment bank SBC Warburg, the Virgin transport and retail group, public transport group National Express Plc, engineering units of France's SNCF, London Electricity Plc and engineering consultants Ove Arup and Halcrow.
